plugins.description: General development workflow skills for committing, branch naming, and other git operations, plus the shared telemetry/v1 emit + validate contract, its stream-generic rollup, and a committed Grafana reference dashboard for the cross-repo hand-off; ships a PreToolUse(Agent) hook, inert unless switch_fable_to_opus is truthy, that then redirects dispatches whose effective model is fable to opus; bootstrap also ships the blessed Spring, non-Spring-Java, Python and Go resilience + dependency-health payloads (resilience4j for the JVM, circuitbreaker+tenacity for Python, sony/gobreaker for Go, wired to the ops-api /health surface â versioned v1/v2, where v2 serves RFC 9457 problem+json on the two probe 503s while v1 stays frozen, #1330). Gathers kubernetes/IaC findings (Helm/Kustomize/Argo CD manifest presence, Kyverno policy + policy-test detection) for the development-kubernetes topic dispatcher, and OpenTofu/Terraform findings (tofu fmt/validate/tflint/trivy presence detection, plus evaluated state-encryption and pinned-Conftest policy + policy-test checks over *.tf) for the development-opentofu topic dispatcher. Bootstrap also ships the no-cluster-deploy required status check, which fails an application repo whose workflows deploy straight to a cluster (the app-repo half of the image-promotion contract). NOTE for existing repos: a re-run of bootstrap now installs ops-api v2 payloads, whose two probe 503s return RFC 9457 problem+json instead of the v1 {"status":"down"} envelope â see the ops-surface how-to before re-running. ALSO for existing repos: bootstrap's .spectral.yaml is now a thin shim extending one EXACT pinned org styleguide ruleset over jsDelivr (#689) instead of the #692 starter, so a re-run replaces a local ruleset with a remote pin and enforces fifteen org rules at error (four of them a warn->error promotion relative to the #692 starter, nine newly minted) â review the api-styleguide how-to before re-running, and note contracts-lint now needs network access to jsDelivr on every run (no offline fallback, by design), so restricted CI egress or a CDN outage fails the lint until it recovers. resolve-issue detects the repo type at Â§1b (review-dispatch.zsh detect) and loads the matching development-<repo_type>:resolve-profile when one exists, continuing with its generic rules when none does (#1504). A human's interactive round grant is now persisted mechanically rather than remembered: record-grant.zsh writes the granted ceiling to <work-dir>/.max-rounds and resolve-story-loop.zsh --resume adopts it, reporting the ceiling in force as the new always-present effective_max_rounds / max_rounds_source status keys while max_rounds keeps reporting the value the caller passed (#1576). Residue condition 2 is removed (#1571): the review loop's CONVERGED_WITH_RESIDUE terminal no longer requires every remaining blocker to sit in the previous round's fix-touched set, because scope-findings already confines each round's findings to the story diff â which made the terminal unreachable from the very closing sweep it was built for, since a promoting round runs no fix pass and its set is empty by design. The terminal is correspondingly BROADER: residue now holds on almost any zero-CRITICAL non-convergence, so runs that previously ended in a human escalation may instead open a PR and file the remainder as follow-up issues - and the #1498 possible-false-trip auto-continue is now tried BEFORE residue at that rung, so the loop still spends its free round rather than shipping. resolve-issue's review loop now hands each reviewer a scope block carrying both the repo-relative and absolute spelling of every file plus a verbatim opener naming the worktree to read, and review-dispatch.zsh plan emits worktree_root/original_root/scope_abs â a repo-root file read from the original checkout produced a CRITICAL false positive (#1582).
